subject: GT M: Integration factory proposal for embed-splitter + fallback lanes
messages:
From: Liam O'Shea <liam@indexfoundry.com>
To: diego.fernandez@redwoodinference.com
Cc: partners@indexfoundry.com
Date: Fri, 7 May 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Integration factory proposal — embed-splitter + fallback lanes

Diego —

Great to meet you at VectorSummit. As discussed, IndexFoundry has a small team that builds connector "factories" for search + embedding pipelines. We put together a short proposal for a joint integration factory that would: 1) provide a turnkey pgvector/S3 fallback connector for customers using Redwood, 2) expose a managed pinecone/weaviate adapter for high-QPS customers, and 3) ship a lightweight SDK for cold-tier retrieval and prefix-KV cache hints.

Attached: IndexFoundry_IntegrationFactory_Deck.pdf (deck with architecture, timelines, and initial commercial options).

High-level asks from our side:
- Technical partnership and an engineer point of contact to scope fallback semantics (pgvector-on-s3 fallback, rehydration windows).
- A PoC window (4 weeks) with a sandbox instance of Redwood Dedicated or a shared test key for throughput tuning.
- GTM alignment: co-branded quickstart + one joint webinar.

Would love to schedule a 30m call next week to walk through the deck and align on MAP (mutual action plan).

Thanks,
Liam O'Shea
Head of Partnerships | IndexFoundry
liam@indexfoundry.com

Attachments: IndexFoundry_IntegrationFactory_Deck.pdf

From: ben.carter@redwoodinference.com
To: diego.fernandez@redwoodinference.com
Cc: vanessa.ortiz@redwoodinference.com, marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com
Date: Mon, 10 May 2027 08:21:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Integration factory proposal — embedding, fallback, commercial sketch

Diego / Vanessa —

I reviewed the deck. Quick internal checklist for the kickoff so we're aligned on asks and avoid scope creep: 

Technical acceptance criteria (provisional):
- Ingest flow: IndexFoundry connector must support incremental writes to pgvector + deterministic spill to S3 (object format defined).
- Read path: Redwood should be able to route at query time: (1) hot index (pgvector/pinecone) -> (2) cold-lane (S3 via pgvector restore) with metadata TTL enforcement.
- Latency target for hot path: p95 < 80ms for 128-token queries at 250 qps sustained in pilot.

Commercial models to propose to partner on kickoff:
- Option A: Pilot rev-share (70/30 Redwood/IndexFoundry) for initial 6 months with a commit floor for host costs.
- Option B: One-time integration engineering fee + certified connector listing in our partner catalog and standard revenue split on referrals.

Ops/Service:
- Who will own rehydration retries and backoff? We should default to connector-owned (IndexFoundry) but Redwood needs a fallback policy for SLA exceptions.
- Observability: connector must emit trace headers + an S3 object metadata mapping file so index transfer reports are observable in Console.

Attachments for meeting: IF_MAP_draft.xlsx (provisional MAP), tech-intake-snapshot.txt (simple checklist). Please review and flag anything that forces legal review (esp. data residency clauses).

-ben
Ben Carter
Director, Partnerships | Redwood Inference
From: Elena Novak <elena@indexfoundry.com>
To: ben.carter@redwoodinference.com, diego.fernandez@redwoodinference.com
Cc: Liam O'Shea <liam@indexfoundry.com>, partners@indexfoundry.com
Date: Wed, 12 May 2027 09:46:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Integration factory proposal — updated MAP and tech notes

Ben / Diego / Vanessa —

Thanks for the checklist — appreciate the clarity. We've updated the MAP and included technical notes inline. Highlights: 
- Rehydration: default window 24h for cold objects, with an optional "fast rehydrate" paid option that caches frequently requested cold keys to a warm bucket.
- Ownership: IndexFoundry will own connector rehydration logic + retry policies; Redwood will expose a fallback policy hook so customers can opt for auto-fallback or strict-fail.
- Security: we commit to per-tenant encryption keys; for EU customers we can support AES keys provided by the customer via KMS.

We've attached the updated MAP and marked two items that will require legal (data residency + audit logs export). Also included a short PoC success metric set: 3 production-like queries, materialization time <= 6s for cold hits, and no data leakage in metadata mapping.

DocuSign link for the MAP acceptance is here: https://www.docusign.net/IF-MAP-2027

Would like to proceed with Tue 11 May 10:00 PT — if that still works, can you send calendar invite?

Best,
Elena Novak
VP Product | IndexFoundry
Attachments: IF_MAP_draft.xlsx, tech-intake-snapshot.txt
